**Gino Paoli** (Italian pronunciation:[[ˈdʒiːno ˈpaːoli]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Italian "Help:IPA/Italian"); 23 September 1934 – 24 March 2026) was an Italian singer-songwriter. He wrote a number of songs widely regarded as classics in [Italian popular music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_popular_music "Italian popular music"), including "[Il cielo in una stanza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Il_cielo_in_una_stanza_(song) "Il cielo in una stanza (song)")", "Che cosa c'è", "[Senza fine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senza_fine "Senza fine")", "Quattro amici" and "[Sapore di sale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sapore_di_sale "Sapore di sale")".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-morto-2)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino_Paoli&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Paoli was born in [Monfalcone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monfalcone "Monfalcone"), near [Trieste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trieste "Trieste"), on 23 September 1934. He moved to [Genoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genoa "Genoa") as a child, where he spent all his life.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-morto-2)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino_Paoli&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

After several different jobs, Paoli was signed to [Dischi Ricordi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dischi_Ricordi "Dischi Ricordi") with friends and fellow musicians Luigi Tenco and [Bruno Lauzi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Lauzi "Bruno Lauzi"), who would constitute, along with Paoli, Umberto Bindi, [Giorgio Calabrese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giorgio_Calabrese "Giorgio Calabrese") and other artists, what is known as the "[Genoese School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genoese_School "Genoese School")" of Italian songwriting.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-morto-2) His first success was the single "[La gatta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_gatta "La gatta")", which has been used in Italian language teaching classes in U.S. middle schools and high schools.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

"[Il cielo in una stanza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Il_cielo_in_una_stanza_(song) "Il cielo in una stanza (song)")" was composed in 1959. According to Paoli, the lyrics came to him while lying on a brothel bed. Gazing at the purple ceiling, he thought, "Love can grow at any moment at any place."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-3)[Mina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mina_(Italian_singer) "Mina (Italian singer)")'s single release of the song topped the list of annual sales in Italy[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-4) and reached the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"). Video performances of the song were included in the movies _Io bacio... tu baci_ and _[Appuntamento a Ischia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appuntamento\_a\_Ischia "Appuntamento a Ischia")_. It was later featured in _[Goodfellas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodfellas "Goodfellas")_. [Carla Bruni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carla_Bruni "Carla Bruni") covered the song (mixing French with her native Italian) on her debut album _[Quelqu'un m'a dit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quelqu'un\_m'a\_dit "Quelqu'un m'a dit")_.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Paoli's debut [album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Album "Album"), _Gino Paoli_, was released in Italy on 8 October 1961 on Dischi Ricordi.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-5) "Il cielo in una stanza" was followed by "[Sapore di sale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sapore_di_sale "Sapore di sale")" (1963), arranged by [Ennio Morricone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ennio_Morricone "Ennio Morricone") and considered to be one of Paoli's most famous songs. In the same year he attempted suicide by shooting himself to the heart (the bullet remained inside his chest).[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 1974, he returned with the LP _I semafori rossi non sono Dio_, followed by _Il mio mestiere_ (1977). Both showed a more mature inspiration than his 1960s works. In the 1980s, Paoli produced a series of successful albums, and in 1985, he toured Italy together with [Ornella Vanoni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ornella_Vanoni "Ornella Vanoni").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 1987, he [was elected](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987_Italian_general_election "1987 Italian general election") to the [Italian Chamber of Deputies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Chamber_of_Deputies "Italian Chamber of Deputies") for the [Italian Communist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Communist_Party "Italian Communist Party"), soon withdrawing from the party to become a left-wing independent.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-6) He abandoned politics in 1992 to pursue his musical ambitions.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino_Paoli&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Paoli had several relationships during his lifetime. He first married Anna Fabbri in 1957, with whom he had a son. After separating, he had a long relationship with actress [Stefania Sandrelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stefania_Sandrelli "Stefania Sandrelli") in the 1960s; their daughter, [Amanda Sandrelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amanda_Sandrelli "Amanda Sandrelli"), is also an actress. He subsequently had an affair with singer [Ornella Vanoni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ornella_Vanoni "Ornella Vanoni"), who remained a close friend of his throughout their lives. Finally, he began dating Paola Penzo of [Modena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modena "Modena") in the 1970s, marrying her in 1991; the couple had three sons.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-morto2-7)

### Legal issues

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino_Paoli&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Legal issues")]

During an interview in February 2015, when a journalist cited a famous phrase of an Italian minister saying that taxes are a good thing, Paoli insulted him.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-8) At the time Paoli was under investigation for tax evasion, accused of having brought €2 million of untaxed income to a Swiss bank.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-9) He was acquitted in 2016.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-10)

### Death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino_Paoli&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Death")]

Paoli died in [Genoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genoa "Genoa") on 24 March 2026, at the age of 91. His last public appearance was at the funeral of Ornella Vanoni the previous November.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-morto-2)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-morto2-7)

**Gino Paoli** (Italian pronunciation:[[ˈdʒiːno ˈpaːoli]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Italian "Help:IPA/Italian"); 23 September 1934 – 24 March 2026) was an Italian singer-songwriter. He wrote a number of songs widely regarded as classics in [Italian popular music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_popular_music "Italian popular music"), including "[Il cielo in una stanza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Il_cielo_in_una_stanza_(song) "Il cielo in una stanza (song)")", "Che cosa c'è", "[Senza fine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senza_fine "Senza fine")", "Quattro amici" and "[Sapore di sale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sapore_di_sale "Sapore di sale")".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-morto-2)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino_Paoli&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Paoli was born in [Monfalcone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monfalcone "Monfalcone"), near [Trieste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trieste "Trieste"), on 23 September 1934. He moved to [Genoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genoa "Genoa") as a child, where he spent all his life.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-morto-2)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino_Paoli&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

After several different jobs, Paoli was signed to [Dischi Ricordi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dischi_Ricordi "Dischi Ricordi") with friends and fellow musicians Luigi Tenco and [Bruno Lauzi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Lauzi "Bruno Lauzi"), who would constitute, along with Paoli, Umberto Bindi, [Giorgio Calabrese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giorgio_Calabrese "Giorgio Calabrese") and other artists, what is known as the "[Genoese School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genoese_School "Genoese School")" of Italian songwriting.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-morto-2) His first success was the single "[La gatta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_gatta "La gatta")", which has been used in Italian language teaching classes in U.S. middle schools and high schools.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

"[Il cielo in una stanza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Il_cielo_in_una_stanza_(song) "Il cielo in una stanza (song)")" was composed in 1959. According to Paoli, the lyrics came to him while lying on a brothel bed. Gazing at the purple ceiling, he thought, "Love can grow at any moment at any place."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-3)[Mina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mina_(Italian_singer) "Mina (Italian singer)")'s single release of the song topped the list of annual sales in Italy[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-4) and reached the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"). Video performances of the song were included in the movies _Io bacio... tu baci_ and _[Appuntamento a Ischia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appuntamento\_a\_Ischia "Appuntamento a Ischia")_. It was later featured in _[Goodfellas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodfellas "Goodfellas")_. [Carla Bruni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carla_Bruni "Carla Bruni") covered the song (mixing French with her native Italian) on her debut album _[Quelqu'un m'a dit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quelqu'un\_m'a\_dit "Quelqu'un m'a dit")_.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Paoli's debut [album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Album "Album"), _Gino Paoli_, was released in Italy on 8 October 1961 on Dischi Ricordi.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-5) "Il cielo in una stanza" was followed by "[Sapore di sale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sapore_di_sale "Sapore di sale")" (1963), arranged by [Ennio Morricone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ennio_Morricone "Ennio Morricone") and considered to be one of Paoli's most famous songs. In the same year he attempted suicide by shooting himself to the heart (the bullet remained inside his chest).[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 1974, he returned with the LP _I semafori rossi non sono Dio_, followed by _Il mio mestiere_ (1977). Both showed a more mature inspiration than his 1960s works. In the 1980s, Paoli produced a series of successful albums, and in 1985, he toured Italy together with [Ornella Vanoni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ornella_Vanoni "Ornella Vanoni").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 1987, he [was elected](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987_Italian_general_election "1987 Italian general election") to the [Italian Chamber of Deputies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Chamber_of_Deputies "Italian Chamber of Deputies") for the [Italian Communist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Communist_Party "Italian Communist Party"), soon withdrawing from the party to become a left-wing independent.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-6) He abandoned politics in 1992 to pursue his musical ambitions.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino_Paoli&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Paoli had several relationships during his lifetime. He first married Anna Fabbri in 1957, with whom he had a son. After separating, he had a long relationship with actress [Stefania Sandrelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stefania_Sandrelli "Stefania Sandrelli") in the 1960s; their daughter, [Amanda Sandrelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amanda_Sandrelli "Amanda Sandrelli"), is also an actress. He subsequently had an affair with singer [Ornella Vanoni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ornella_Vanoni "Ornella Vanoni"), who remained a close friend of his throughout their lives. Finally, he began dating Paola Penzo of [Modena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modena "Modena") in the 1970s, marrying her in 1991; the couple had three sons.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-morto2-7)

### Legal issues

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino_Paoli&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Legal issues")]

During an interview in February 2015, when a journalist cited a famous phrase of an Italian minister saying that taxes are a good thing, Paoli insulted him.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-8) At the time Paoli was under investigation for tax evasion, accused of having brought €2 million of untaxed income to a Swiss bank.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-9) He was acquitted in 2016.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-10)

### Death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gino_Paoli&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Death")]

Paoli died in [Genoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genoa "Genoa") on 24 March 2026, at the age of 91. His last public appearance was at the funeral of Ornella Vanoni the previous November.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-morto-2)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Paoli#cite_note-morto2-7)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Italian organist and lyricist (1905–1969)

**Antonio Allegra** (1905 – 1969) was an Italian [organist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organist "Organist") and [lyricist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyricist "Lyricist"). As one of the organists of [St. Peter's Basilica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Peter's_Basilica "St. Peter's Basilica") at his time, he wrote the words to _[Inno e Marcia Pontificale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inno\_e\_Marcia\_Pontificale "Inno e Marcia Pontificale")_, which was adopted in 1949 as the [national anthem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_anthem "National anthem") of the [Holy See](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_See "Holy See") ([Vatican City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatican_City "Vatican City")).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Allegra#cite_note-1) The music was by [Charles Gounod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Gounod "Charles Gounod").

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Italian organist and lyricist (1905–1969)

**Antonio Allegra** (1905 – 1969) was an Italian [organist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organist "Organist") and [lyricist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyricist "Lyricist"). As one of the organists of [St. Peter's Basilica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Peter's_Basilica "St. Peter's Basilica") at his time, he wrote the words to _[Inno e Marcia Pontificale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inno\_e\_Marcia\_Pontificale "Inno e Marcia Pontificale")_, which was adopted in 1949 as the [national anthem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_anthem "National anthem") of the [Holy See](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_See "Holy See") ([Vatican City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatican_City "Vatican City")).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Allegra#cite_note-1) The music was by [Charles Gounod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Gounod "Charles Gounod").

Musical artist

**Renato Carosone** (Italian pronunciation:[[reˈnaːto karoˈzoːne]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Italian "Help:IPA/Italian"); born **Renato Carusone**; 3 January 1920 – 20 May 2001) was an Italian musician.

Carosone was a piano prodigy and prominent figure in the [Italian music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_of_Italy "Music of Italy") scene in the second half of the 20th century. He was also a modern performer of the so-called [canzone napoletana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canzone_napoletana "Canzone napoletana"), a traditional music genre from [Naples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naples "Naples"). His biggest successes were: "'O sarracino/Caravan petrol", "[Tu vuò fà l'americano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tu_vu%C3%B2_f%C3%A0_l'americano "Tu vuò fà l'americano")", "Maruzzella" and "Pigliate 'na pastiglia".

Carosone was one of the first post-war Italian artists (the other one being [Domenico Modugno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domenico_Modugno "Domenico Modugno")) who sold records and toured in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") without singing in English.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renato_Carosone#cite_note-1)

## Biography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Renato_Carosone&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]

### Beginnings

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Renato_Carosone&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Beginnings")]

Carosone was born on 3 January 1920 in [Naples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naples "Naples"), in Vico dei Tornieri, near [Piazza del Mercato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza_del_Mercato?action=edit&redlink=1 "Piazza del Mercato (page does not exist)")[[it](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza%20del%20Mercato%20(Napoli) "it:Piazza del Mercato (Napoli)")], to Antonio and Carolina Daino, along with sister Olga and brother Ottavio. His father, who worked in the box office at [Teatro Mercadante](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teatro_Mercadante "Teatro Mercadante"), encouraged him to pursue music. At 14, he wrote "Triki-trak", his first composition for piano, and in 1935, he was hired by an _[opera dei pupi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opera\_dei\_pupi "Opera dei pupi")_ puppet theater to play music to the battles of Count [Roland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roland "Roland") and [Renaud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renaud_de_Montauban "Renaud de Montauban"). Subsequently, he worked at [E. A. Mario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E._A._Mario "E. A. Mario")'s publishing house teaching new songs to singers. He studied piano and [composition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_composition "Musical composition") at the [Naples Conservatory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naples_Conservatory "Naples Conservatory") under [Alberto Curci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alberto_Curci?action=edit&redlink=1 "Alberto Curci (page does not exist)")[[it](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alberto%20Curci "it:Alberto Curci")], and obtained his diploma in 1937, when he was just 17.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renato_Carosone#cite_note-2)

A few months later he signed a contract with comedian Aldo Russo to perform as a [band leader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Band_leader "Band leader") in [Italian East Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_East_Africa "Italian East Africa"). The troup landed in [Massawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massawa "Massawa"), [Eritrea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eritrea_Governorate "Eritrea Governorate"), to work in a restaurant-theatre frequented by Italian workers. The act failed and after less than a week, Aldo Russo decided to dissolve the group and return to Naples. Carosone, however, decided to remain in East Africa, and he moved on to [Asmara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asmara "Asmara") in the Eritrean highlands, playing piano in an orchestra at the Circolo Italia. There he met and fell in love with Venetian dancer Italia Levidi, known as Lita. The two married in Massawa on 2 January 1938. Carosone adopted her son Giuseppe, known as Pino, born to Lita five years before the wedding. Shortly thereafter, Carosone moved to [Addis Ababa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Addis_Ababa "Addis Ababa") (now part of Ethiopia), where he spent a few months as conductor at the White Eagle. In June 1940, at the outbreak of [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), he was called up and sent to [the front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_African_campaign_(World_War_II) "East African campaign (World War II)") in [Italian Somaliland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somalia_Governorate "Somalia Governorate").

Following the surrender of the last regular Italian forces in the region in November 1941, Carosone returned to [British-occupied](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Eritrea "British Eritrea") Asmara, where his cousin Antonio was director of the Odeon Theatre. Carosone then became the musical director of the theater and the adjoining nightclub. He was a prominent figure of the local music scene, performing a combination of big-band music, Neapolitan songs and Eritrean percussive elements.

Carosone worked at the Odeon Club in Asmara, where he became a prominent figure of the local music scene, building his musical experience with a combination of [big-band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big-band "Big-band") music (including American [dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_dance "Social dance") pieces, such as "[Night and Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Night_and_Day_(song) "Night and Day (song)")", "[Begin the Beguine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Begin_the_Beguine "Begin the Beguine")", "[Blue Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Moon_(1934_song) "Blue Moon (1934 song)")" and "[Tea for Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tea_for_Two_(song) "Tea for Two (song)")"), Neapolitan songs and Eritrean percussive elements.

In July 1946, after the end of the war in Europe, he returned to Italy, to [Brindisi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brindisi "Brindisi"), with his wife and son. Partially due to his long tenure abroad and inactivity caused by the war, Carosone was discovered to be virtually unknown in his home country. He started his career afresh, playing piano for small dance-hall bands. These new performances were strongly influenced by the new rhythms and music styles he had encountered during his ten years in East Africa and caught the attention of local promoters.

### Success

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Renato_Carosone&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Success")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c5/Renato_Carosone_mentre_autografa.jpg/250px-Renato_Carosone_mentre_autografa.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Renato_Carosone_mentre_autografa.jpg)

Renato Carosone in the fifties

In 1949 Carosone was asked to put together a band for a club's opening night. After some auditions, he signed the Dutch [guitarist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guitarist "Guitarist")[Peter van Houten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Van_Wood "Peter Van Wood") and the Neapolitan [drummer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drummer "Drummer")[Gegè Di Giacomo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geg%C3%A8_Di_Giacomo "Gegè Di Giacomo") and formed the [Trio Carosone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trio_Carosone?action=edit&redlink=1 "Trio Carosone (page does not exist)"). The trio would later become a quartet with the addition of the [Hungarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarians "Hungarians")[romani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romani_people "Romani people") musician [Elek Bacsik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elek_Bacsik "Elek Bacsik") on bass, guitar and violin.

During the 1950s Carosone became more and more popular, his orchestra was in great demand both in Italy and abroad, and record sales were soaring high.

His song "Torero", entered the pop charts in the United States in the summer of 1958 where it peaked at #18, making it his only Top 20 hit song for his [one-hit wonder in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_one-hit_wonders_in_the_United_States "List of one-hit wonders in the United States"). "Torero" was translated into twelve languages and covered by almost thirty artists in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") alone, including versions by [The Andrews Sisters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Andrews_Sisters "The Andrews Sisters"), [Connie Francis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connie_Francis "Connie Francis") and [The King Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_King_Brothers "The King Brothers").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renato_Carosone#cite_note-3) In 1957 Carosone and his band embarked on an American tour, kicking off in [Cuba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba "Cuba"). This tour concluded with a triumphant performance at the prestigious [Carnegie Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnegie_Hall "Carnegie Hall") in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renato_Carosone#cite_note-4)

Carosone was then signed by [Capitol Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capitol_Records "Capitol Records"), which released his first two albums: _Honeymoon in Rome_ (1957) and _Renato Carosone!_ (1959). He then moved to [Pathé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Path%C3%A9 "Pathé") and recorded _Blue Italian Skies_ (1958). His fourth studio album, _Carnevale Carosone_ (1960) was released by [Parlophone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parlophone "Parlophone").

### Retirement

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Renato_Carosone&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Retirement")]

At the height of his career, Carosone announced his retirement from music in 1960. He felt that the advent of [Rock and roll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_roll "Rock and roll") had the consequence of making his swing, big-band sound no longer popular: "I'd rather retire now on the crest of the wave, than being tormented later by the idea of rock and roll wiping away all that I have achieved in so many years of hard work".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renato_Carosone#cite_note-5) His decision to retire caused an uproar. Some observers even suspected obscure underworld threats. Away from the spotlight, Carosone turned to other interests, mainly [painting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Painting "Painting"). In 2007 the [Castel Sant'Angelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castel_Sant'Angelo "Castel Sant'Angelo") Museum in [Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rome "Rome") organized a large exhibition of his work.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renato_Carosone#cite_note-6)

### Comeback

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Renato_Carosone&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Comeback")]

On 9 August 1975 Carosone made his comeback in a [televised](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TV "TV") concert. He then resumed his musical career with live concerts, performances at the [Sanremo Music Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanremo_Music_Festival "Sanremo Music Festival") and TV appearances until the late 1990s.

## Repertoire

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Renato_Carosone&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Repertoire")]

The majority of Carosone's songs were the result of his long and fruitful collaboration with the [lyricist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyricist "Lyricist")[Nicola Salerno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicola_Salerno "Nicola Salerno"), who used the [pseudonym](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pseudonym "Pseudonym") Nisa. "'O suspiro", "Torero", "[Tu vuò fà l'americano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tu_vu%C3%B2_f%C3%A0_l'americano "Tu vuò fà l'americano")", "[Mambo italiano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mambo_Italiano "Mambo Italiano")", "Pigliate 'na pastiglia" and "'O sarracino/Caravan petrol" were among their greatest hits.

A few famous songs not co-written by Nisa were "...E la barca tornò sola" (a parody of a song performed by [Gino Latilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Latilla "Gino Latilla") at Sanremo Music Festival in 1954); "Tre numeri al lotto"; "Maruzzella" (dedicated to his wife); and "'O russo e 'a rossa"

## Death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Renato_Carosone&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Death")]

Carosone died on 20 May 2001 at the age of 81 in [Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rome "Rome"), Italy.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renato_Carosone#cite_note-7)

Musical artist

**Renato Carosone** (Italian pronunciation:[[reˈnaːto karoˈzoːne]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Italian "Help:IPA/Italian"); born **Renato Carusone**; 3 January 1920 – 20 May 2001) was an Italian musician.

Carosone was a piano prodigy and prominent figure in the [Italian music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_of_Italy "Music of Italy") scene in the second half of the 20th century. He was also a modern performer of the so-called [canzone napoletana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canzone_napoletana "Canzone napoletana"), a traditional music genre from [Naples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naples "Naples"). His biggest successes were: "'O sarracino/Caravan petrol", "[Tu vuò fà l'americano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tu_vu%C3%B2_f%C3%A0_l'americano "Tu vuò fà l'americano")", "Maruzzella" and "Pigliate 'na pastiglia".

Carosone was one of the first post-war Italian artists (the other one being [Domenico Modugno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domenico_Modugno "Domenico Modugno")) who sold records and toured in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") without singing in English.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renato_Carosone#cite_note-1)

## Biography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Renato_Carosone&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]

### Beginnings

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Renato_Carosone&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Beginnings")]

Carosone was born on 3 January 1920 in [Naples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naples "Naples"), in Vico dei Tornieri, near [Piazza del Mercato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza_del_Mercato?action=edit&redlink=1 "Piazza del Mercato (page does not exist)")[[it](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piazza%20del%20Mercato%20(Napoli) "it:Piazza del Mercato (Napoli)")], to Antonio and Carolina Daino, along with sister Olga and brother Ottavio. His father, who worked in the box office at [Teatro Mercadante](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teatro_Mercadante "Teatro Mercadante"), encouraged him to pursue music. At 14, he wrote "Triki-trak", his first composition for piano, and in 1935, he was hired by an _[opera dei pupi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opera\_dei\_pupi "Opera dei pupi")_ puppet theater to play music to the battles of Count [Roland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roland "Roland") and [Renaud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renaud_de_Montauban "Renaud de Montauban"). Subsequently, he worked at [E. A. Mario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E._A._Mario "E. A. Mario")'s publishing house teaching new songs to singers. He studied piano and [composition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_composition "Musical composition") at the [Naples Conservatory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naples_Conservatory "Naples Conservatory") under [Alberto Curci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alberto_Curci?action=edit&redlink=1 "Alberto Curci (page does not exist)")[[it](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alberto%20Curci "it:Alberto Curci")], and obtained his diploma in 1937, when he was just 17.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renato_Carosone#cite_note-2)

A few months later he signed a contract with comedian Aldo Russo to perform as a [band leader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Band_leader "Band leader") in [Italian East Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_East_Africa "Italian East Africa"). The troup landed in [Massawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massawa "Massawa"), [Eritrea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eritrea_Governorate "Eritrea Governorate"), to work in a restaurant-theatre frequented by Italian workers. The act failed and after less than a week, Aldo Russo decided to dissolve the group and return to Naples. Carosone, however, decided to remain in East Africa, and he moved on to [Asmara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asmara "Asmara") in the Eritrean highlands, playing piano in an orchestra at the Circolo Italia. There he met and fell in love with Venetian dancer Italia Levidi, known as Lita. The two married in Massawa on 2 January 1938. Carosone adopted her son Giuseppe, known as Pino, born to Lita five years before the wedding. Shortly thereafter, Carosone moved to [Addis Ababa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Addis_Ababa "Addis Ababa") (now part of Ethiopia), where he spent a few months as conductor at the White Eagle. In June 1940, at the outbreak of [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), he was called up and sent to [the front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_African_campaign_(World_War_II) "East African campaign (World War II)") in [Italian Somaliland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somalia_Governorate "Somalia Governorate").

Following the surrender of the last regular Italian forces in the region in November 1941, Carosone returned to [British-occupied](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Eritrea "British Eritrea") Asmara, where his cousin Antonio was director of the Odeon Theatre. Carosone then became the musical director of the theater and the adjoining nightclub. He was a prominent figure of the local music scene, performing a combination of big-band music, Neapolitan songs and Eritrean percussive elements.

Carosone worked at the Odeon Club in Asmara, where he became a prominent figure of the local music scene, building his musical experience with a combination of [big-band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big-band "Big-band") music (including American [dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_dance "Social dance") pieces, such as "[Night and Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Night_and_Day_(song) "Night and Day (song)")", "[Begin the Beguine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Begin_the_Beguine "Begin the Beguine")", "[Blue Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Moon_(1934_song) "Blue Moon (1934 song)")" and "[Tea for Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tea_for_Two_(song) "Tea for Two (song)")"), Neapolitan songs and Eritrean percussive elements.

In July 1946, after the end of the war in Europe, he returned to Italy, to [Brindisi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brindisi "Brindisi"), with his wife and son. Partially due to his long tenure abroad and inactivity caused by the war, Carosone was discovered to be virtually unknown in his home country. He started his career afresh, playing piano for small dance-hall bands. These new performances were strongly influenced by the new rhythms and music styles he had encountered during his ten years in East Africa and caught the attention of local promoters.

### Success

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Renato_Carosone&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Success")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c5/Renato_Carosone_mentre_autografa.jpg/250px-Renato_Carosone_mentre_autografa.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Renato_Carosone_mentre_autografa.jpg)

Renato Carosone in the fifties

In 1949 Carosone was asked to put together a band for a club's opening night. After some auditions, he signed the Dutch [guitarist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guitarist "Guitarist")[Peter van Houten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Van_Wood "Peter Van Wood") and the Neapolitan [drummer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drummer "Drummer")[Gegè Di Giacomo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geg%C3%A8_Di_Giacomo "Gegè Di Giacomo") and formed the [Trio Carosone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trio_Carosone?action=edit&redlink=1 "Trio Carosone (page does not exist)"). The trio would later become a quartet with the addition of the [Hungarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarians "Hungarians")[romani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romani_people "Romani people") musician [Elek Bacsik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elek_Bacsik "Elek Bacsik") on bass, guitar and violin.

During the 1950s Carosone became more and more popular, his orchestra was in great demand both in Italy and abroad, and record sales were soaring high.

His song "Torero", entered the pop charts in the United States in the summer of 1958 where it peaked at #18, making it his only Top 20 hit song for his [one-hit wonder in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_one-hit_wonders_in_the_United_States "List of one-hit wonders in the United States"). "Torero" was translated into twelve languages and covered by almost thirty artists in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") alone, including versions by [The Andrews Sisters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Andrews_Sisters "The Andrews Sisters"), [Connie Francis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connie_Francis "Connie Francis") and [The King Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_King_Brothers "The King Brothers").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renato_Carosone#cite_note-3) In 1957 Carosone and his band embarked on an American tour, kicking off in [Cuba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba "Cuba"). This tour concluded with a triumphant performance at the prestigious [Carnegie Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnegie_Hall "Carnegie Hall") in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renato_Carosone#cite_note-4)

Carosone was then signed by [Capitol Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capitol_Records "Capitol Records"), which released his first two albums: _Honeymoon in Rome_ (1957) and _Renato Carosone!_ (1959). He then moved to [Pathé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Path%C3%A9 "Pathé") and recorded _Blue Italian Skies_ (1958). His fourth studio album, _Carnevale Carosone_ (1960) was released by [Parlophone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parlophone "Parlophone").

### Retirement

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Renato_Carosone&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Retirement")]

At the height of his career, Carosone announced his retirement from music in 1960. He felt that the advent of [Rock and roll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_roll "Rock and roll") had the consequence of making his swing, big-band sound no longer popular: "I'd rather retire now on the crest of the wave, than being tormented later by the idea of rock and roll wiping away all that I have achieved in so many years of hard work".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renato_Carosone#cite_note-5) His decision to retire caused an uproar. Some observers even suspected obscure underworld threats. Away from the spotlight, Carosone turned to other interests, mainly [painting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Painting "Painting"). In 2007 the [Castel Sant'Angelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castel_Sant'Angelo "Castel Sant'Angelo") Museum in [Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rome "Rome") organized a large exhibition of his work.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renato_Carosone#cite_note-6)

### Comeback

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Renato_Carosone&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Comeback")]

On 9 August 1975 Carosone made his comeback in a [televised](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TV "TV") concert. He then resumed his musical career with live concerts, performances at the [Sanremo Music Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanremo_Music_Festival "Sanremo Music Festival") and TV appearances until the late 1990s.

## Repertoire

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Renato_Carosone&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Repertoire")]

The majority of Carosone's songs were the result of his long and fruitful collaboration with the [lyricist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyricist "Lyricist")[Nicola Salerno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicola_Salerno "Nicola Salerno"), who used the [pseudonym](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pseudonym "Pseudonym") Nisa. "'O suspiro", "Torero", "[Tu vuò fà l'americano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tu_vu%C3%B2_f%C3%A0_l'americano "Tu vuò fà l'americano")", "[Mambo italiano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mambo_Italiano "Mambo Italiano")", "Pigliate 'na pastiglia" and "'O sarracino/Caravan petrol" were among their greatest hits.

A few famous songs not co-written by Nisa were "...E la barca tornò sola" (a parody of a song performed by [Gino Latilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Latilla "Gino Latilla") at Sanremo Music Festival in 1954); "Tre numeri al lotto"; "Maruzzella" (dedicated to his wife); and "'O russo e 'a rossa"

## Death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Renato_Carosone&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Death")]

Carosone died on 20 May 2001 at the age of 81 in [Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rome "Rome"), Italy.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renato_Carosone#cite_note-7)

**Nicola Salerno** (11 March 1910 – 22 May 1969), often known as **Nisa**, was an Italian lyricist. He formed a famous [songwriting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Songwriter "Songwriter") duo with Renato Carosone.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicola_Salerno#cite_note-1)

## Life and career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nicola_Salerno&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Life and career")]

Nicola Salerno was born in [Naples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naples "Naples") in 1910.

His first hit was "Eulalia Torricelli" of 1947, about the unhappy love story between a wealthy girl from [Forlì](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forl%C3%AC "Forlì") and a guy named Giosuè. Salerno put the whole team of songwriters (including himself, [Gino Redi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Redi "Gino Redi") and [Dino Olivieri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dino_Olivieri "Dino Olivieri")) in the lyrics as heirs to each of Eulalia's three castles.

Salerno met Renato Carosone in 1955. It was Mariano Rapetti, [Ricordi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_Ricordi "Casa Ricordi") record company's director – and father of lyricist [Mogol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mogol_(lyricist) "Mogol (lyricist)") – who suggested that they should work together to enter a radio contest. Nisa brought Carosone three texts to be set to music. One of them was titled "[Tu vuò fà l'americano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tu_vu%C3%B2_f%C3%A0_l'americano "Tu vuò fà l'americano")". Carosone had an instant inspiration and started composing a [boogie-woogie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boogie-woogie "Boogie-woogie") on the piano keyboard. It took just fifteen minutes to create Carosone's most famous song, that became a worldwide success. Other famous hits by the duo include "'O suspiro", "Torero", "Caravan Petrol", "Pigliate 'na pastiglia" and "'O sarracino".

Salerno worked also with other songwriters. Among his best-known lyrics are "[Guaglione](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guaglione "Guaglione")", winning song of the [Naples Song Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Festival_di_Napoli "Festival di Napoli") in 1956, and "[Non ho l'età](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non_ho_l'et%C3%A0 "Non ho l'età")", with which [Gigliola Cinquetti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gigliola_Cinquetti "Gigliola Cinquetti") won both the [Sanremo Music Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanremo_Music_Festival_1964 "Sanremo Music Festival 1964") and the [Eurovision Song Contest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurovision_Song_Contest_1964 "Eurovision Song Contest 1964") in 1964.

Besides writing lyrics, Nicola Salerno was also an [illustrator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illustrator "Illustrator"). He was the author, for example, of cover designs for some [Neapolitan music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_of_Naples "Music of Naples") scores published between the 1920s and 1930s.

He died in Naples in 1969. His son [Alberto Salerno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alberto_Salerno "Alberto Salerno") would also become a successful lyricist.

**Nicola Salerno** (11 March 1910 – 22 May 1969), often known as **Nisa**, was an Italian lyricist. He formed a famous [songwriting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Songwriter "Songwriter") duo with Renato Carosone.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicola_Salerno#cite_note-1)

## Life and career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nicola_Salerno&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Life and career")]

Nicola Salerno was born in [Naples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naples "Naples") in 1910.

His first hit was "Eulalia Torricelli" of 1947, about the unhappy love story between a wealthy girl from [Forlì](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forl%C3%AC "Forlì") and a guy named Giosuè. Salerno put the whole team of songwriters (including himself, [Gino Redi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gino_Redi "Gino Redi") and [Dino Olivieri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dino_Olivieri "Dino Olivieri")) in the lyrics as heirs to each of Eulalia's three castles.

Salerno met Renato Carosone in 1955. It was Mariano Rapetti, [Ricordi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_Ricordi "Casa Ricordi") record company's director – and father of lyricist [Mogol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mogol_(lyricist) "Mogol (lyricist)") – who suggested that they should work together to enter a radio contest. Nisa brought Carosone three texts to be set to music. One of them was titled "[Tu vuò fà l'americano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tu_vu%C3%B2_f%C3%A0_l'americano "Tu vuò fà l'americano")". Carosone had an instant inspiration and started composing a [boogie-woogie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boogie-woogie "Boogie-woogie") on the piano keyboard. It took just fifteen minutes to create Carosone's most famous song, that became a worldwide success. Other famous hits by the duo include "'O suspiro", "Torero", "Caravan Petrol", "Pigliate 'na pastiglia" and "'O sarracino".

Salerno worked also with other songwriters. Among his best-known lyrics are "[Guaglione](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guaglione "Guaglione")", winning song of the [Naples Song Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Festival_di_Napoli "Festival di Napoli") in 1956, and "[Non ho l'età](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non_ho_l'et%C3%A0 "Non ho l'età")", with which [Gigliola Cinquetti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gigliola_Cinquetti "Gigliola Cinquetti") won both the [Sanremo Music Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanremo_Music_Festival_1964 "Sanremo Music Festival 1964") and the [Eurovision Song Contest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurovision_Song_Contest_1964 "Eurovision Song Contest 1964") in 1964.

Besides writing lyrics, Nicola Salerno was also an [illustrator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illustrator "Illustrator"). He was the author, for example, of cover designs for some [Neapolitan music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_of_Naples "Music of Naples") scores published between the 1920s and 1930s.

He died in Naples in 1969. His son [Alberto Salerno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alberto_Salerno "Alberto Salerno") would also become a successful lyricist.

Musical artist

**Mario Merola** (Italian pronunciation:[[ˈmaːrjo ˈmɛːrola]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Italian "Help:IPA/Italian"); 6 April, 1934 – 12 November, 2006) was an Italian singer and actor. He has been nicknamed "The King of the [Sceneggiata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sceneggiata "Sceneggiata")" (Italian: _il Re della sceneggiata_), a type of regional drama originating in Naples and later finding more widespread recognition.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-1)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mario_Merola_(singer)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]

Mario Merola began his career as a [longshoreman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dockworker "Dockworker") at the [Port of Naples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Naples "Port of Naples"). His first public singing performance occurred by chance, when he sang during a celebration of the [Virgin Mary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary,_mother_of_Jesus "Mary, mother of Jesus"), at the church of Sant’Anna alle Paludi when the scheduled singer, [Mario Trevi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Trevi "Mario Trevi"), was delayed.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-2)

In 1964, he first performed at the [Festival of Naples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Festival_of_Naples "Festival of Naples") with the song _Doce è ’o silenzio_ (“Sweet is the silence”), with Elsa Quarta.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-3)

He performed at the festival a number of times in the 1960-70s. He also performed and won in 2001, performing _L’urdemo emigrante_ (“The Last Emigrant”) with his son Francesco.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-4)

He recorded about 40 records of _sceneggiata_ music and had additional credits in filmed versions. He toured abroad with a Neapolitan company to present the _sceneggiata_ to [emigrant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emigration "Emigration") Italian communities. During the 1970s, Merola performed at the [White House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House "White House"), showcasing the Neapolitan genre.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-5)

In addition to his own music career, Merola was a [talent scout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talent_scout "Talent scout"), contributing to the early careers of [Massimo Ranieri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massimo_Ranieri "Massimo Ranieri"), [Nino D'Angelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_D'Angelo "Nino D'Angelo"), and [Gigi D'Alessio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gigi_D'Alessio "Gigi D'Alessio"), among others.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-6)

At the [Sanremo Music Festival 1994](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanremo_Music_Festival_1994 "Sanremo Music Festival 1994"), he formed "Team Italy", performing "Una vecchia canzone italiana" (“An Old Italian Song”) with [Nilla Pizzi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilla_Pizzi "Nilla Pizzi"), [Wess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wess "Wess"), [Wilma Goich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilma_Goich "Wilma Goich"), [Manuela Villa](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuela%20Villa "it:Manuela Villa"), [Tony Santagata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Santagata "Tony Santagata"), [Jimmy Fontana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Fontana "Jimmy Fontana"), [Gianni Nazzaro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gianni_Nazzaro "Gianni Nazzaro"), [Lando Fiorini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lando_Fiorini "Lando Fiorini"), [Rosanna Fratello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosanna_Fratello "Rosanna Fratello"), and [Giuseppe Cionfoli](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giuseppe%20Cionfoli "it:Giuseppe Cionfoli"). The group recorded an album of the same name, featuring collective and individual recordings.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-7)

## Personal life and death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mario_Merola_(singer)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Personal life and death")]

Merola married Rosa Serrapiglia on 5 April, 1964. They had three children: Roberto (a musical events organizer), Loredana (a homemaker), and Francesco (a singer), who occasionally performed alongside his father.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-8)

In 1997, Merola was hospitalized for three weeks at Naples’ Vecchio Pellegrini Hospital for a cardiorespiratory crisis. He subsequently recovered.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-9)

On 26 November, 2005, Merola was appointed a [Knight of Malta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sovereign_Military_Order_of_Malta "Sovereign Military Order of Malta"), alongside [Bruno Venturini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Venturini "Bruno Venturini") and [Mario Trevi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Trevi "Mario Trevi").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-10)

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/74/La_Tomba_di_Mario_Merola.jpg/250px-La_Tomba_di_Mario_Merola.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:La_Tomba_di_Mario_Merola.jpg)

Merola's gravestone in Naples

Merola died on November 12, 2006, at the age of 72 in [Castellammare di Stabia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castellammare_di_Stabia "Castellammare di Stabia"), after breathing difficulties.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-11)

His funeral was held on November 14, 2006, at the Basilica of Santa Maria del Carmine Maggiore in Naples in the same church where he was married. It was attended by family, political figures, and professional colleagues. An estimated 40,000 people gathered outside. A large number followed the procession to his burial at the Monumental Cemetery of Naples.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-12)

## Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mario_Merola_(singer)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Legacy")]

During the [Sanremo Festival 2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanremo_Music_Festival_2000 "Sanremo Music Festival 2000"), [Bono](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bono "Bono") of [U2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U2 "U2") fell into the crowd during a performance and encountered Mario Merola.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-13)

In 2004, [Hugo Race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugo_Race "Hugo Race") released _The Merola Matrix_, an album of 16 songs using excerpts from some of Merola's older songs and film scenes.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-14)

In 2008, the restaurant‑museum _Felicissima sera_ (“Very happy evening”) opened in Naples, displaying photos, objects and memorabilia related to the singer. It also includes a letter written by [Eduardo De Filippo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eduardo_De_Filippo "Eduardo De Filippo") to Merola dated 29 October 1976.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-15) His children, Roberto and Francesco, collaborated with designer Nadia Wanderlingh among others.

In 2009, a commemorative bust of Merola was erected in the Sant’Anna alle Paludi district of Naples. Created by sculptor Domenico Sepe, it bears the inscription: “Mario Merola, ambassador of Neapolitan songs in the world.”[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-17)

On 18 September, 2010, a memorial concert for Merola was held at the Stadio San Ciro in [Portici](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portici "Portici"), featuring, among others, Francesco Merola, [Tullio De Piscopo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tullio_De_Piscopo "Tullio De Piscopo"), [Sal Da Vinci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sal_Da_Vinci "Sal Da Vinci"), Gigi Finizio, Gianni Fiorellino, [Mario Da Vinci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Da_Vinci "Mario Da Vinci"), Valentina Stella, Gloriana, and [Gigi D'Alessio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gigi_D'Alessio "Gigi D'Alessio").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-18)

Musical artist

**Mario Merola** (Italian pronunciation:[[ˈmaːrjo ˈmɛːrola]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Italian "Help:IPA/Italian"); 6 April, 1934 – 12 November, 2006) was an Italian singer and actor. He has been nicknamed "The King of the [Sceneggiata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sceneggiata "Sceneggiata")" (Italian: _il Re della sceneggiata_), a type of regional drama originating in Naples and later finding more widespread recognition.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-1)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mario_Merola_(singer)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]

Mario Merola began his career as a [longshoreman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dockworker "Dockworker") at the [Port of Naples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Naples "Port of Naples"). His first public singing performance occurred by chance, when he sang during a celebration of the [Virgin Mary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary,_mother_of_Jesus "Mary, mother of Jesus"), at the church of Sant’Anna alle Paludi when the scheduled singer, [Mario Trevi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Trevi "Mario Trevi"), was delayed.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-2)

In 1964, he first performed at the [Festival of Naples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Festival_of_Naples "Festival of Naples") with the song _Doce è ’o silenzio_ (“Sweet is the silence”), with Elsa Quarta.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-3)

He performed at the festival a number of times in the 1960-70s. He also performed and won in 2001, performing _L’urdemo emigrante_ (“The Last Emigrant”) with his son Francesco.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-4)

He recorded about 40 records of _sceneggiata_ music and had additional credits in filmed versions. He toured abroad with a Neapolitan company to present the _sceneggiata_ to [emigrant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emigration "Emigration") Italian communities. During the 1970s, Merola performed at the [White House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House "White House"), showcasing the Neapolitan genre.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-5)

In addition to his own music career, Merola was a [talent scout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talent_scout "Talent scout"), contributing to the early careers of [Massimo Ranieri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massimo_Ranieri "Massimo Ranieri"), [Nino D'Angelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_D'Angelo "Nino D'Angelo"), and [Gigi D'Alessio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gigi_D'Alessio "Gigi D'Alessio"), among others.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-6)

At the [Sanremo Music Festival 1994](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanremo_Music_Festival_1994 "Sanremo Music Festival 1994"), he formed "Team Italy", performing "Una vecchia canzone italiana" (“An Old Italian Song”) with [Nilla Pizzi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilla_Pizzi "Nilla Pizzi"), [Wess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wess "Wess"), [Wilma Goich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilma_Goich "Wilma Goich"), [Manuela Villa](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuela%20Villa "it:Manuela Villa"), [Tony Santagata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Santagata "Tony Santagata"), [Jimmy Fontana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Fontana "Jimmy Fontana"), [Gianni Nazzaro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gianni_Nazzaro "Gianni Nazzaro"), [Lando Fiorini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lando_Fiorini "Lando Fiorini"), [Rosanna Fratello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosanna_Fratello "Rosanna Fratello"), and [Giuseppe Cionfoli](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giuseppe%20Cionfoli "it:Giuseppe Cionfoli"). The group recorded an album of the same name, featuring collective and individual recordings.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-7)

## Personal life and death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mario_Merola_(singer)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Personal life and death")]

Merola married Rosa Serrapiglia on 5 April, 1964. They had three children: Roberto (a musical events organizer), Loredana (a homemaker), and Francesco (a singer), who occasionally performed alongside his father.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-8)

In 1997, Merola was hospitalized for three weeks at Naples’ Vecchio Pellegrini Hospital for a cardiorespiratory crisis. He subsequently recovered.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-9)

On 26 November, 2005, Merola was appointed a [Knight of Malta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sovereign_Military_Order_of_Malta "Sovereign Military Order of Malta"), alongside [Bruno Venturini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Venturini "Bruno Venturini") and [Mario Trevi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Trevi "Mario Trevi").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-10)

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/74/La_Tomba_di_Mario_Merola.jpg/250px-La_Tomba_di_Mario_Merola.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:La_Tomba_di_Mario_Merola.jpg)

Merola's gravestone in Naples

Merola died on November 12, 2006, at the age of 72 in [Castellammare di Stabia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castellammare_di_Stabia "Castellammare di Stabia"), after breathing difficulties.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-11)

His funeral was held on November 14, 2006, at the Basilica of Santa Maria del Carmine Maggiore in Naples in the same church where he was married. It was attended by family, political figures, and professional colleagues. An estimated 40,000 people gathered outside. A large number followed the procession to his burial at the Monumental Cemetery of Naples.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-12)

## Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mario_Merola_(singer)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Legacy")]

During the [Sanremo Festival 2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanremo_Music_Festival_2000 "Sanremo Music Festival 2000"), [Bono](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bono "Bono") of [U2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U2 "U2") fell into the crowd during a performance and encountered Mario Merola.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-13)

In 2004, [Hugo Race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugo_Race "Hugo Race") released _The Merola Matrix_, an album of 16 songs using excerpts from some of Merola's older songs and film scenes.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-14)

In 2008, the restaurant‑museum _Felicissima sera_ (“Very happy evening”) opened in Naples, displaying photos, objects and memorabilia related to the singer. It also includes a letter written by [Eduardo De Filippo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eduardo_De_Filippo "Eduardo De Filippo") to Merola dated 29 October 1976.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-15) His children, Roberto and Francesco, collaborated with designer Nadia Wanderlingh among others.

In 2009, a commemorative bust of Merola was erected in the Sant’Anna alle Paludi district of Naples. Created by sculptor Domenico Sepe, it bears the inscription: “Mario Merola, ambassador of Neapolitan songs in the world.”[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-17)

On 18 September, 2010, a memorial concert for Merola was held at the Stadio San Ciro in [Portici](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portici "Portici"), featuring, among others, Francesco Merola, [Tullio De Piscopo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tullio_De_Piscopo "Tullio De Piscopo"), [Sal Da Vinci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sal_Da_Vinci "Sal Da Vinci"), Gigi Finizio, Gianni Fiorellino, [Mario Da Vinci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Da_Vinci "Mario Da Vinci"), Valentina Stella, Gloriana, and [Gigi D'Alessio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gigi_D'Alessio "Gigi D'Alessio").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merola_(singer)#cite_note-18)

**Saturnino** "**Nino**" **Manfredi** (22 March 1921 – 4 June 2004) was an Italian actor, voice actor, director, screenwriter, playwright, comedian, singer, author, radio personality and television presenter.

He was one of the most prominent Italian actors in the [commedia all'italiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commedia_all'italiana "Commedia all'italiana") genre. During his career he won several awards, including six [David di Donatello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_di_Donatello "David di Donatello") awards, six [Nastro d'Argento](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nastro_d'Argento "Nastro d'Argento") awards and the Prix de la première oeuvre (Best First Work Award) at the [1971 Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1971_Cannes_Film_Festival "1971 Cannes Film Festival") for _[Between Miracles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Between\_Miracles "Between Miracles")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-premi-1) Typically playing losers, marginalised, working-class characters yet "in possession of their dignity, morality, and underlying optimism",[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-deed-2) he was referred to as "one of the few truly complete actors in Italian cinema".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-deed-2)

## Life and career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nino_Manfredi&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Life and career")]

### Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nino_Manfredi&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early life")]

Manfredi was born in [Castro dei Volsci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castro_dei_Volsci "Castro dei Volsci"), [Frosinone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Province_of_Frosinone "Province of Frosinone") into a humble family of farmers.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3) His father recruited in [Public Safety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_safety "Public safety"), where he reached the rank of [Maresciallo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maresciallo "Maresciallo"), and in the early 1930s, he was transferred to Rome, where Nino and his younger brother Dante spent their childhood in the popular neighborhood of San Giovanni.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3) In 1937, he became seriously ill with [bilateral pleurisy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleurisy "Pleurisy"), and after a doctor gave him only three months to live,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Debenedetti-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Nudo_d'attore-5) he remained several years hospitalized in a [sanatorium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanatorium "Sanatorium"); there he learned to play a [banjo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banjo "Banjo") built by himself and he entered the musical band of the hospital.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Nudo_d'attore-5) To please his family in October 1941, he enrolled at the university in the Faculty of Law, but already in the same year he showed an interest and a natural inclination for the stage, making his debut as a presenter and an actor in the theater of a parish in Rome.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3)

After 8 September 1943, in order to avoid conscription, he took refuge for a year with his brother in the mountains above [Cassino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassino "Cassino");[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3) returned to Rome in 1944, he resumed his university studies and, at the same time, he enrolled at the [National Academy of Dramatic Art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accademia_Nazionale_di_Arte_Drammatica_Silvio_D'Amico "Accademia Nazionale di Arte Drammatica Silvio D'Amico").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3) In October 1945, he graduated in law with a thesis in [criminal law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Criminal_law "Criminal law"), without ever practicing the profession, and in June 1947, he graduated from the academy.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3)

### First successes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nino_Manfredi&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: First successes")]

In 1958, Manfredi got his first film role as the main actor.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3) The same year he formed a revue company with [Delia Scala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delia_Scala "Delia Scala") and [Paolo Panelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_Panelli "Paolo Panelli"), getting some success with the musical _Un trapezio per Lisistrata_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3) In 1959, the trio was chosen by [RAI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RAI "RAI") to host _[Canzonissima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canzonissima "Canzonissima")_; the show marked the turning point of the career of Manfredi, who enjoyed a very large popularity, mainly thanks to the "[macchietta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macchietta "Macchietta")" (i.e. comic caricature) of the "Barman from [Ceccano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceccano "Ceccano")".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3) The success immediately got him a contract with [Dino De Laurentiis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dino_De_Laurentiis "Dino De Laurentiis") which he dropped after one year to be free to choose his favorite projects.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3)

In 1962, Manfredi enjoyed an even larger success playing the title role in the stage musical _[Rugantino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rugantino\_(musical) "Rugantino (musical)")_, with which he toured also in Canada, the US, and Argentina.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3) The same year he directed the critically appreciated segment "L'avventura di un soldato" in the [anthology film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthology_film "Anthology film")_[Of Wayward Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Of\_Wayward\_Love "Of Wayward Love")_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3) In 1963 he starred in [Luis García Berlanga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Garc%C3%ADa_Berlanga "Luis García Berlanga")'s masterpiece _[The Executioner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Executioner\_(1963\_film) "The Executioner (1963 film)")_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-6)

### Commedia all'italiana icon

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nino_Manfredi&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Commedia all'italiana icon")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/73/Manfredi_nell%27anno_del_Signore.jpg/250px-Manfredi_nell%27anno_del_Signore.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Manfredi_nell'anno_del_Signore.jpg)

Manfredi in _[Nell'anno del Signore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nell'anno\_del\_Signore "Nell'anno del Signore")_ (1969)

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f5/Geppetto_Manfredi.jpg/250px-Geppetto_Manfredi.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Geppetto_Manfredi.jpg)

Manfredi as Geppetto in the TV series _[The Adventures of Pinocchio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Adventures\_of\_Pinocchio\_(1972\_miniseries) "The Adventures of Pinocchio (1972 miniseries)")_ (1972)

Starting from the second half of the 1960s, Manfredi became a top actor at the Italian box office, starring in some of the most successful and critically acclaimed films in the [Commedia all'italiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commedia_all'italiana "Commedia all'italiana") genre, often directed by [Dino Risi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dino_Risi "Dino Risi").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Giacovelli-7) In 1969, with _[Nell'anno del Signore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nell'anno\_del\_Signore "Nell'anno del Signore")_, he started a fruitful collaboration with the director [Luigi Magni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luigi_Magni "Luigi Magni").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Giacovelli-7) In the same period he started collaborating, often uncredited, to the screenplays of his films.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3)

In 1970, he enjoyed a large musical success with the [Ettore Petrolini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ettore_Petrolini "Ettore Petrolini")'s song "Tanto pe' cantà"; the song premiered, out of competition, at the [Sanremo Music Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanremo_Music_Festival "Sanremo Music Festival") and it peaked at third place on the Italian hit parade.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-hitparade-8) In 1971, he made his feature film debut as director with the semi-autobiographical _[Between Miracles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Between\_Miracles "Between Miracles")_, with which he got almost unanimous critical acclaim, winning the Best Film Work Award at the [Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannes_Film_Festival "Cannes Film Festival"), the [Italian Golden Globe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Golden_Globe "Italian Golden Globe") for Best First Feature, two [Silver Ribbons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_Ribbon "Silver Ribbon") (for best screenplay and best original story) and a special [David di Donatello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_di_Donatello "David di Donatello").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3) In 1972 he got a major television success playing [Geppetto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geppetto "Geppetto") in the [Luigi Comencini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luigi_Comencini "Luigi Comencini")'s adaptation _[The Adventures of Pinocchio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Adventures\_of\_Pinocchio\_(1972\_miniseries) "The Adventures of Pinocchio (1972 miniseries)")_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Grasso-9) In the 1970s and early 1980s, he continued alternating high-profile works and less ambitious comedies; among the most successful performances of the time, the emarginated immigrant of _[Bread and Chocolate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bread\_and\_Chocolate "Bread and Chocolate")_ (1973), the idealist worker of _[We All Loved Each Other So Much](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We\_All\_Loved\_Each\_Other\_So\_Much "We All Loved Each Other So Much")_ (1974), the old [shanty town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanty_town "Shanty town") patriarch of _[Down and Dirty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Down\_and\_Dirty\_(film) "Down and Dirty (film)")_ (1976), the [Vatican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatican_City "Vatican City")'s magistrate of _[In the Name of the Pope King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In\_the\_Name\_of\_the\_Pope\_King "In the Name of the Pope King")_ (1977), the abusive coffee-seller in _[Café Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caf%C3%A9\_Express\_(film) "Café Express (film)")_ (1980).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Giacovelli-7)
