### Later career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nino_Manfredi&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Later career")]

Following his last film as director (_[Portrait of a Woman, Nude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portrait\_of\_a\_Woman,\_Nude "Portrait of a Woman, Nude")_) and two commercial hit films starred alongside [Renato Pozzetto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renato_Pozzetto "Renato Pozzetto") (_[Heads I Win, Tails You Lose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heads\_I\_Win,\_Tails\_You\_Lose "Heads I Win, Tails You Lose")_ and _[Questo e Quello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Questo\_e\_Quello "Questo e Quello")_), in the 1980s, Manfredi significantly slowed his cinema activities.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3)

In 1983, he debuted as an author with the book _Proverbi e altre cose romanesche_, while in 1984, he signed his first work as playwright and stage director (_Viva gli sposi_), an activity in which he gradually focused.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3) In 1990 he received a [David di Donatello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_di_Donatello "David di Donatello") career award.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3) In 1992, after having first accepted to be a candidate at the elections with the [Pannella List](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pannella_List "Pannella List"), he withdrew his candidature to not give up his artistic commitments.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-10) In 1993, during the shooting of _[Un commissario a Roma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Un\_commissario\_a\_Roma "Un commissario a Roma")_, he suffered a [hypoxia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypoxia_(medical) "Hypoxia (medical)") which compromised his [memory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memory "Memory") functions.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-11) Starting from _Un commissario a Roma_ his popularity revamped thanks to a series of successful [RAI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RAI "RAI") TV-series and miniseries, notably _[Linda e il brigadiere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linda\_e\_il\_brigadiere "Linda e il brigadiere")_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Grasso-9)

### Last role and death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nino_Manfredi&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Last role and death")]

Manfredi's last role was Galapago, an almost mute stranger with no memory in [Miguel Hermoso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miguel_Hermoso "Miguel Hermoso")'s Spanish drama film _[The End of a Mystery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_End\_of\_a\_Mystery "The End of a Mystery")_. On 7 July 2003, a few months after the release of the film, he was struck by a [cerebral infarction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerebral_infarction "Cerebral infarction") in his home in Rome.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-intensiva-12) In August, he received a Career Bianchi Prize at the [Venice Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venice_Film_Festival "Venice Film Festival").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-13) In September, an improvement allowed him to return home, but in December, he was hit by a new cerebral haemorrhage.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-intensiva-12) After spending six months in a continuous alternation of improvements and deteriorations, he died on 4 June 2004, aged eighty-three years old.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-14)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nino_Manfredi&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Personal life")]

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/17/Viale_Nino_Manfredi.JPG/250px-Viale_Nino_Manfredi.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Viale_Nino_Manfredi.JPG)

"Viale Nino Manfredi", a street named after him in Rome

Manfredi was married to model Erminia Ferrari from 1955 till his death. The couple had a son, Luca (who is a film and television director), and two daughters, Roberta (an actress, television presenter and producer) and Giovanna.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3) He had another daughter, Tonina, from a Bulgarian woman.

From an early age, Manfredi suffered from a [biliary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biliary "Biliary") disorder, which forced him to a very strict diet, and his meals often consisted of just light tea or [caffè d'orzo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caff%C3%A8_d'orzo "Caffè d'orzo").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Tornabuoni-15) He was an atheist.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Tornabuoni-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-16) Active in volunteering, in 1991, he was nominated [Goodwill Ambassador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodwill_Ambassador "Goodwill Ambassador") for [UNICEF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNICEF "UNICEF").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3)

## Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nino_Manfredi&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Legacy")]

In 2007, an asteroid ([73453 Ninomanfredi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/73453_Ninomanfredi "73453 Ninomanfredi")) was named after him.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-17) In 2009, a Nino Manfredi Prize was established at the [Nastro d’Argento Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nastro_d'Argento "Nastro d'Argento").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-18) Manfredi also named a theatre in [Ostia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ostia_(Rome) "Ostia (Rome)"), Rome.

On the occasion of the tenth anniversary of his death, in 2014, Manfredi was remembered by "Nino!", a series of events, held in various places including Los Angeles, New York, Rome and Paris, which included retrospectives, exhibitions, and the staging of an unreleased play of Manfredi.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-19)

In 2017, his son Luca Manfredi directed a biographical film about Manfredi's early years, _In arte Nino_; Manfredi was played by [Elio Germano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elio_Germano "Elio Germano"), while [Miriam Leone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miriam_Leone "Miriam Leone") played his wife Erminia.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-21)

**Saturnino** "**Nino**" **Manfredi** (22 March 1921 – 4 June 2004) was an Italian actor, voice actor, director, screenwriter, playwright, comedian, singer, author, radio personality and television presenter.

He was one of the most prominent Italian actors in the [commedia all'italiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commedia_all'italiana "Commedia all'italiana") genre. During his career he won several awards, including six [David di Donatello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_di_Donatello "David di Donatello") awards, six [Nastro d'Argento](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nastro_d'Argento "Nastro d'Argento") awards and the Prix de la première oeuvre (Best First Work Award) at the [1971 Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1971_Cannes_Film_Festival "1971 Cannes Film Festival") for _[Between Miracles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Between\_Miracles "Between Miracles")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-premi-1) Typically playing losers, marginalised, working-class characters yet "in possession of their dignity, morality, and underlying optimism",[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-deed-2) he was referred to as "one of the few truly complete actors in Italian cinema".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-deed-2)

## Life and career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nino_Manfredi&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Life and career")]

### Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nino_Manfredi&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early life")]

Manfredi was born in [Castro dei Volsci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castro_dei_Volsci "Castro dei Volsci"), [Frosinone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Province_of_Frosinone "Province of Frosinone") into a humble family of farmers.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3) His father recruited in [Public Safety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_safety "Public safety"), where he reached the rank of [Maresciallo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maresciallo "Maresciallo"), and in the early 1930s, he was transferred to Rome, where Nino and his younger brother Dante spent their childhood in the popular neighborhood of San Giovanni.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3) In 1937, he became seriously ill with [bilateral pleurisy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleurisy "Pleurisy"), and after a doctor gave him only three months to live,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Debenedetti-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Nudo_d'attore-5) he remained several years hospitalized in a [sanatorium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanatorium "Sanatorium"); there he learned to play a [banjo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banjo "Banjo") built by himself and he entered the musical band of the hospital.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Nudo_d'attore-5) To please his family in October 1941, he enrolled at the university in the Faculty of Law, but already in the same year he showed an interest and a natural inclination for the stage, making his debut as a presenter and an actor in the theater of a parish in Rome.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3)

After 8 September 1943, in order to avoid conscription, he took refuge for a year with his brother in the mountains above [Cassino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassino "Cassino");[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3) returned to Rome in 1944, he resumed his university studies and, at the same time, he enrolled at the [National Academy of Dramatic Art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accademia_Nazionale_di_Arte_Drammatica_Silvio_D'Amico "Accademia Nazionale di Arte Drammatica Silvio D'Amico").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3) In October 1945, he graduated in law with a thesis in [criminal law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Criminal_law "Criminal law"), without ever practicing the profession, and in June 1947, he graduated from the academy.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3)

### Early career

### First successes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nino_Manfredi&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: First successes")]

In 1958, Manfredi got his first film role as the main actor.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3) The same year he formed a revue company with [Delia Scala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delia_Scala "Delia Scala") and [Paolo Panelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_Panelli "Paolo Panelli"), getting some success with the musical _Un trapezio per Lisistrata_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3) In 1959, the trio was chosen by [RAI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RAI "RAI") to host _[Canzonissima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canzonissima "Canzonissima")_; the show marked the turning point of the career of Manfredi, who enjoyed a very large popularity, mainly thanks to the "[macchietta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macchietta "Macchietta")" (i.e. comic caricature) of the "Barman from [Ceccano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceccano "Ceccano")".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3) The success immediately got him a contract with [Dino De Laurentiis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dino_De_Laurentiis "Dino De Laurentiis") which he dropped after one year to be free to choose his favorite projects.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3)

In 1962, Manfredi enjoyed an even larger success playing the title role in the stage musical _[Rugantino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rugantino\_(musical) "Rugantino (musical)")_, with which he toured also in Canada, the US, and Argentina.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3) The same year he directed the critically appreciated segment "L'avventura di un soldato" in the [anthology film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthology_film "Anthology film")_[Of Wayward Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Of\_Wayward\_Love "Of Wayward Love")_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3) In 1963 he starred in [Luis García Berlanga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Garc%C3%ADa_Berlanga "Luis García Berlanga")'s masterpiece _[The Executioner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Executioner\_(1963\_film) "The Executioner (1963 film)")_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-6)

### Commedia all'italiana icon

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nino_Manfredi&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Commedia all'italiana icon")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/73/Manfredi_nell%27anno_del_Signore.jpg/250px-Manfredi_nell%27anno_del_Signore.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Manfredi_nell'anno_del_Signore.jpg)

Manfredi in _[Nell'anno del Signore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nell'anno\_del\_Signore "Nell'anno del Signore")_ (1969)

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f5/Geppetto_Manfredi.jpg/250px-Geppetto_Manfredi.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Geppetto_Manfredi.jpg)

Manfredi as Geppetto in the TV series _[The Adventures of Pinocchio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Adventures\_of\_Pinocchio\_(1972\_miniseries) "The Adventures of Pinocchio (1972 miniseries)")_ (1972)

Starting from the second half of the 1960s, Manfredi became a top actor at the Italian box office, starring in some of the most successful and critically acclaimed films in the [Commedia all'italiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commedia_all'italiana "Commedia all'italiana") genre, often directed by [Dino Risi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dino_Risi "Dino Risi").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Giacovelli-7) In 1969, with _[Nell'anno del Signore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nell'anno\_del\_Signore "Nell'anno del Signore")_, he started a fruitful collaboration with the director [Luigi Magni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luigi_Magni "Luigi Magni").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Giacovelli-7) In the same period he started collaborating, often uncredited, to the screenplays of his films.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3)

In 1970, he enjoyed a large musical success with the [Ettore Petrolini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ettore_Petrolini "Ettore Petrolini")'s song "Tanto pe' cantà"; the song premiered, out of competition, at the [Sanremo Music Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanremo_Music_Festival "Sanremo Music Festival") and it peaked at third place on the Italian hit parade.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-hitparade-8) In 1971, he made his feature film debut as director with the semi-autobiographical _[Between Miracles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Between\_Miracles "Between Miracles")_, with which he got almost unanimous critical acclaim, winning the Best Film Work Award at the [Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannes_Film_Festival "Cannes Film Festival"), the [Italian Golden Globe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Golden_Globe "Italian Golden Globe") for Best First Feature, two [Silver Ribbons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_Ribbon "Silver Ribbon") (for best screenplay and best original story) and a special [David di Donatello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_di_Donatello "David di Donatello").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3) In 1972 he got a major television success playing [Geppetto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geppetto "Geppetto") in the [Luigi Comencini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luigi_Comencini "Luigi Comencini")'s adaptation _[The Adventures of Pinocchio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Adventures\_of\_Pinocchio\_(1972\_miniseries) "The Adventures of Pinocchio (1972 miniseries)")_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Grasso-9) In the 1970s and early 1980s, he continued alternating high-profile works and less ambitious comedies; among the most successful performances of the time, the emarginated immigrant of _[Bread and Chocolate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bread\_and\_Chocolate "Bread and Chocolate")_ (1973), the idealist worker of _[We All Loved Each Other So Much](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We\_All\_Loved\_Each\_Other\_So\_Much "We All Loved Each Other So Much")_ (1974), the old [shanty town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanty_town "Shanty town") patriarch of _[Down and Dirty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Down\_and\_Dirty\_(film) "Down and Dirty (film)")_ (1976), the [Vatican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatican_City "Vatican City")'s magistrate of _[In the Name of the Pope King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In\_the\_Name\_of\_the\_Pope\_King "In the Name of the Pope King")_ (1977), the abusive coffee-seller in _[Café Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caf%C3%A9\_Express\_(film) "Café Express (film)")_ (1980).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Giacovelli-7)

### Later career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nino_Manfredi&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Later career")]

Following his last film as director (_[Portrait of a Woman, Nude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portrait\_of\_a\_Woman,\_Nude "Portrait of a Woman, Nude")_) and two commercial hit films starred alongside [Renato Pozzetto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renato_Pozzetto "Renato Pozzetto") (_[Heads I Win, Tails You Lose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heads\_I\_Win,\_Tails\_You\_Lose "Heads I Win, Tails You Lose")_ and _[Questo e Quello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Questo\_e\_Quello "Questo e Quello")_), in the 1980s, Manfredi significantly slowed his cinema activities.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3)

In 1983, he debuted as an author with the book _Proverbi e altre cose romanesche_, while in 1984, he signed his first work as playwright and stage director (_Viva gli sposi_), an activity in which he gradually focused.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3) In 1990 he received a [David di Donatello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_di_Donatello "David di Donatello") career award.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3) In 1992, after having first accepted to be a candidate at the elections with the [Pannella List](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pannella_List "Pannella List"), he withdrew his candidature to not give up his artistic commitments.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-10) In 1993, during the shooting of _[Un commissario a Roma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Un\_commissario\_a\_Roma "Un commissario a Roma")_, he suffered a [hypoxia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypoxia_(medical) "Hypoxia (medical)") which compromised his [memory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memory "Memory") functions.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-11) Starting from _Un commissario a Roma_ his popularity revamped thanks to a series of successful [RAI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RAI "RAI") TV-series and miniseries, notably _[Linda e il brigadiere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linda\_e\_il\_brigadiere "Linda e il brigadiere")_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Grasso-9)

### Last role and death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nino_Manfredi&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Last role and death")]

Manfredi's last role was Galapago, an almost mute stranger with no memory in [Miguel Hermoso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miguel_Hermoso "Miguel Hermoso")'s Spanish drama film _[The End of a Mystery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_End\_of\_a\_Mystery "The End of a Mystery")_. On 7 July 2003, a few months after the release of the film, he was struck by a [cerebral infarction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerebral_infarction "Cerebral infarction") in his home in Rome.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-intensiva-12) In August, he received a Career Bianchi Prize at the [Venice Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venice_Film_Festival "Venice Film Festival").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-13) In September, an improvement allowed him to return home, but in December, he was hit by a new cerebral haemorrhage.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-intensiva-12) After spending six months in a continuous alternation of improvements and deteriorations, he died on 4 June 2004, aged eighty-three years old.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-14)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nino_Manfredi&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Personal life")]

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/17/Viale_Nino_Manfredi.JPG/250px-Viale_Nino_Manfredi.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Viale_Nino_Manfredi.JPG)

"Viale Nino Manfredi", a street named after him in Rome

Manfredi was married to model Erminia Ferrari from 1955 till his death. The couple had a son, Luca (who is a film and television director), and two daughters, Roberta (an actress, television presenter and producer) and Giovanna.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3) He had another daughter, Tonina, from a Bulgarian woman.

From an early age, Manfredi suffered from a [biliary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biliary "Biliary") disorder, which forced him to a very strict diet, and his meals often consisted of just light tea or [caffè d'orzo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caff%C3%A8_d'orzo "Caffè d'orzo").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Tornabuoni-15) He was an atheist.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Tornabuoni-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-16) Active in volunteering, in 1991, he was nominated [Goodwill Ambassador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodwill_Ambassador "Goodwill Ambassador") for [UNICEF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNICEF "UNICEF").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-Bernardini-3)

## Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nino_Manfredi&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Legacy")]

In 2007, an asteroid ([73453 Ninomanfredi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/73453_Ninomanfredi "73453 Ninomanfredi")) was named after him.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-17) In 2009, a Nino Manfredi Prize was established at the [Nastro d’Argento Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nastro_d'Argento "Nastro d'Argento").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-18) Manfredi also named a theatre in [Ostia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ostia_(Rome) "Ostia (Rome)"), Rome.

On the occasion of the tenth anniversary of his death, in 2014, Manfredi was remembered by "Nino!", a series of events, held in various places including Los Angeles, New York, Rome and Paris, which included retrospectives, exhibitions, and the staging of an unreleased play of Manfredi.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-19)

In 2017, his son Luca Manfredi directed a biographical film about Manfredi's early years, _In arte Nino_; Manfredi was played by [Elio Germano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elio_Germano "Elio Germano"), while [Miriam Leone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miriam_Leone "Miriam Leone") played his wife Erminia.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Manfredi#cite_note-21)
